title: Add a dark theme and a compact mode
prompt:
The light theme and the components are done. Add two modes by remapping semantic tokens only (leave the components alone):

- **Dark theme** for any element with `data-theme="dark"`, not just `<html>`: surface → `--nw-gray-950`, text → `--nw-gray-100`, action background → `--nw-blue-400`, action text → `--nw-gray-950`. Also set `color-scheme: dark`.
- **Compact density** for `data-density="compact"`: control padding y → `--nw-space-1`, x → `--nw-space-3`.

The hero section already carries `data-theme="dark"`, so it should turn dark as soon as your theme works.
hints: Use attribute selectors on their own: `[data-theme="dark"] { … }`. Adding `html` in front would stop the hero from matching.
Inside the block, redeclare the four semantic color tokens with `var()` pointing at the dark primitives.
The density block only needs `--nw-space-control-y` and `--nw-space-control-x`.
explanation: Both modes are pure remappings: no component CSS changed, yet the hero card, its button and any page with `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` all switch. Because the selector is a bare attribute selector, the theme can start at any element, and because the button declares its component tokens on `.nw-button`, they resolve against the nearest theme. Density owns only spacing tokens, so it combines with either theme without extra rules.

checks.light-default: The page stays light by default
checks.hero-dark: The hero card (inside `data-theme="dark"`) uses the dark surface and text
checks.dark-button: Buttons inside the dark hero use the lighter blue with dark text
checks.page-dark: `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` darkens the whole page and sets `color-scheme: dark`
checks.compact: `data-density="compact"` shrinks the button padding to 4px by 12px
